Read FACETS results for standalone visualization and fit review

Source: R/api-facets-results.R
read_facets_results.Rd

Import reported element measures, fit statistics and optional Graphfile curves without refitting a model. Use plot.mfrm_facets_results() to inspect the saved results, or pass the returned object to facets_fit_review() for external FACETS-vs-mfrmr fit comparison.

Usage

read_facets_results(
  file = NULL,
  facet = NULL,
  facet_map = NULL,
  format = c("auto", "delimited", "scorefile"),
  facet_col = NULL,
  level_col = NULL,
  delimiter = NULL,
  encoding = "UTF-8",
  source_version = NULL,
  measure_units = NULL,
  common_scale = FALSE,
  graph_file = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facets_results'
summary(object, ..., component = c("elements", "curves"))

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facets_results'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facets_results'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  component = c("elements", "curves")
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_facets_results'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("measure", "wright", "fit", "infit_outfit", "ccc", "expected"),
  facets = NULL,
  statistic = c("infit", "outfit"),
  draw = TRUE,
  show_title = FALSE,
  show_notes = FALSE,
  show_legend = TRUE,
  scales = NULL,
  label_map = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

file

Scorefile input (a vector of file paths, a directory containing score.N.txt files, or a data frame), or NULL when only graph_file is supplied.

facet

Optional facet name to assign when the file does not contain a facet column. Use this for one-facet CSV exports.

facet_map

Optional character vector mapping FACETS score-file numbers to facet names, for example c("1" = "Person", "2" = "Rater"). If unnamed, positions are used as score-file numbers.

format

File format. "auto" detects FACETS score.N.txt files from their name/header; "delimited" reads a CSV/TSV/semicolon table; and "scorefile" reads a FACETS score-file table, including comma, tab or semicolon exports with facet heading lines. Fixed-field input requires validated all-field headings with element number after the statistics; appended facet fields are separated from the element label. Headerless, element-first and selected-field fixed layouts are rejected. Use named delimited columns for those layouts and for non-ASCII labels.

facet_col, level_col

Optional explicit column names for delimited tables when automatic detection is not sufficient. For score files, level_col can override the column immediately before F-Number.

delimiter

Optional delimiter for delimited tables. If omitted, comma, tab, and semicolon are detected from the header line.

encoding

Source file encoding, explicitly converted to UTF-8.

source_version

Optional FACETS version recorded with these exports. Unknown versions remain NA; the reader does not infer a version.

measure_units

Optional description of the reported measure units, after checking FACETS reporting transformations. Unknown units remain NA.

common_scale

Logical; explicitly declare that the imported facets have compatible units and origins for a shared-axis Wright map. Defaults to false. This declaration does not transform, center or reverse measures.

graph_file

Optional path to one FACETS Graphfile with headings, in CSV, tab-separated or validated ASCII fixed-width format. Supply an export from the same analysis when also importing element results. File identity is recorded, but the reader cannot certify that the exports belong together.

object

A saved mfrm_facets_results object.

...

Must be empty.

component

"elements" (default) or "curves" for Graphfile results.

x

Saved output of read_facets_results().

Also for summary(): A saved mfrm_facets_results object.

row.names

Optional row names for the exported data frame.

optional

Passed to as.data.frame().

type

"measure" for labelled element locations by facet; "wright" for points by facet on one measure axis; "fit" for measure versus mean square; or "infit_outfit" for Infit versus Outfit. Wright maps require the explicit common_scale = TRUE declaration at import. "ccc" plots Graphfile category probabilities and "expected" plots Graphfile expected scores, each in separate scale panels.

facets

Optional character vector of facet names to display.

statistic

"infit" or "outfit", used for type = "fit".

draw

Logical; print the ggplot figure when true.

show_title, show_notes

Logical; show title/interpretation notes in the plot, off by default. Notes always remain in the returned data.

show_legend

Logical; display the source-status symbol key or category curve key below the panels. Defaults to true.

scales

Optional vector of Graphfile scale numbers for curve plots. Facet selectors do not apply to curves, and scale selectors do not apply to element plots.

label_map

Optional data frame with character columns Facet, ElementID and DisplayLabel for element plots. Keys must match exported IDs in x, including any leading zeros, and must be unique within a facet. A partial map is allowed; unmapped rows retain their source labels. Mapping is checked against the full result before facets selection. This changes display labels only, not source labels or element identity. Curve plots do not accept this map. Only type = "measure" draws element labels; the other element plots retain them in returned plot data.

Value

A mfrm_facets_results list with table (all imported rows, source tokens, IDs, status and per-quantity availability), sources (file paths, MD5 checksums and encoding; unavailable for data frames), metadata (source declarations) and notes. When supplied, graph contains the original character table, long curves with raw tokens, precision and availability, row-level diagnostics, categories and detected layout. Graph metadata identifies its separate coordinate system; its units remain unknown rather than inheriting element measure_units. summary() counts available rows by facet. AnchorFlagged counts SourceStatus = "anchored" rows, not individually fixed parameters; it replaces the earlier candidate's ambiguous Anchored summary column. as.data.frame() exports the element table. Use component = "curves" with either method to inspect Graphfile curves. Use saveRDS() to retain the full object.

For plot(): Invisibly a ggplot object whose underlying payload (accessible via plot_data()) retains every selected row in plot_data with X, Y, Available and Reason; element plots also have Symbol, and curves have Series, Color, LineType and Segment. Unavailable numerical coordinates are NA (measure plots retain label positions). Original reported values/status remain in the same rows. notes, sources and metadata describe interpretation and origin. label_map retains a supplied display map. Filtering and display labels do not change the saved results.

Details

Each file must describe one analysis. Supply a vector of facet files or a directory containing score.N.txt files, or a named delimited table. Comma, tab and semicolon Scorefiles retain their native facet heading lines. Numeric facet numbers default to Facet1, Facet2, etc.; supply facet_map to name them. A data frame is also accepted. Validated fixed-field Scorefile layouts and named delimited tables are supported; use named delimited files for non-ASCII labels because byte and character widths can differ. For text output from FACETS, request Scorefile=score.txt, Heading lines=Yes, QM=Double and CSV=Commas, Tabs or Semicolons. Check that the files were actually generated; a zero process exit code alone does not establish a successful export. Specify the encoding of the existing file; the reader does not configure FACETS input encoding or repair labels already lost during export. Element IDs are preserved separately from display labels. Where no ID was exported, the label is the key; ambiguous duplicate keys are rejected, not averaged. Unknown source status remains unknown.

FACETS status codes distinguish anchor-flagged, estimated, extreme, no-data, unmeasurable and single-observation elements. StatusRaw = "1" and the retained SourceStatus = "anchored" mean an anchor flag, not proof that the individual measure was fixed. FACETS 4.5.0 uses this flag for estimated group-anchor members as well as direct anchors and singleton groups. GroupRaw can also describe a reporting group; it does not establish the anchor subtype. Neither a group's imported size nor a reported SE resolves that ambiguity. Check the original Labels= specification for the anchor mode and Table 7 for row annotations. A Table 7 G annotation alone need not distinguish the G and X input modes. This reader does not parse those sources or infer a subtype. Extreme group members can instead carry Status -2/-3, so AnchorFlagged does not count every member of an anchored group. Finite extreme measures are retained as reported locations, not ordinary finite maximum-likelihood estimates. The status alone does not identify their adjustment rule: native X group anchoring can report a different location from G anchoring. Reported fit values for extremes can be placeholders, so their fit plots are unavailable. No-data and unmeasurable elements remain in the returned table. Missing or censored values are never replaced with zero. Marginal source SEs are retained for inspection, but do not supply joint covariance or validated confidence intervals. The object contains no likelihood, response data, inferred thresholds, new-person scoring or calibration-inclusive inference.

Source measures, signs and rounding are retained. A positive or negative sign describes the source model contribution; the plot does not multiply measures by that sign. Check the original specification before interpreting severity, ability or comparing facet origins. Reading results does not validate their convergence, model fit or substantive interpretation.

Graphfiles preserve the reported Scale, Measure, Expected, ExpCat and Prob:<category> fields. Scale numbers identify Table 8 subtables, not automatically items or facets. Category labels can differ from response codes (including binary exports labelled 1/2); no recoding is performed. Expected is used directly, not recomputed from probabilities or ExpCat. The Graphfile Measure axis is not automatically a Person ability axis or the coordinate system of Scorefile measures; measure_units and common_scale apply only to element plots.

Graph imports require unambiguous headings and strictly monotone distinct finite measures within each scale. Missing coordinates/values are retained with reasons and break curve lines. Probability sums are checked against the sum of half the printed units of precision, plus floating-point tolerance; sums outside that rounding allowance are withheld from probability plots. Incomplete probability vectors remain flagged, with available individual probabilities retained. Nothing is renormalized, smoothed or extrapolated. These are source-consistency checks, not validation of the fitted model.

plot() method: Plot imported FACETS measures, fit statistics and curves

For plot(): Each measure panel has its own axis; the Wright display shares one measure axis without centering, reversing signs or inventing category thresholds. Filled circles denote estimated elements, squares direct/group anchor flags, downward/upward triangles extreme low/high source status, diamonds single observations and open circles unknown source status. The symbol key is in plot_data(p, "legend"). A square marks source Status 1; it does not identify an individually fixed measure. Group-anchor members can vary around a fixed group mean, and GroupRaw may instead be a reporting group. Check the original specification or Table 7 to distinguish direct and group anchors. Returned notes retain this limitation, also when plotting imports saved by an earlier version; the source object is not changed. Recreate saved plot-data objects with plot() to obtain the revised legend and notes. Duplicate display labels are disambiguated by element key in measure plots. Use label_map to display local names while retaining the original FACETS labels and IDs. It cannot recover names lost in an export; supply the known correspondence yourself. Character preservation and font rendering are separate: choose an installed font with the required glyphs on the graphics device. With Cairo support, grDevices::png() with type = "cairo" and grDevices::cairo_pdf() accept a family such as "Meiryo" on Windows when installed. Font availability differs across systems. The plot does not install fonts or change global font settings. Infit/Outfit reference lines at one describe the model reference, not a fairness or acceptability cutoff. No confidence bars are calculated. Extreme/single-observation fit placeholders and unmeasurable/no-data elements are retained as unavailable. A plot can have no usable points; inspect its row-level reasons. Unknown status is displayed explicitly, not certified. Graphfile curves join consecutive exported coordinates with straight line segments; this does not calculate new model predictions. Missing or invalid rows break the lines. The legend identifies source category labels. Expected scores and category labels retain their source coding. Each panel has its own reported Measure axis, independent of element-plot scale declarations. For curves, plot_data(p, "data") holds the raw Graphfile table, plot_data(p, "plot_data") the selected long rows, and plot_data(p, "diagnostics") the probability-sum checks.

References

FACETS Scorefile specification: https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/scoreoutput.htm. FACETS Graphfile specification: https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/graphfile.htm. FACETS element and Table 7 anchor annotations: https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/elements.htm and https://www.winsteps.com/facetman64/table7.htm.

Examples

# Small synthetic binary-rating analysis exported by FACETS.
# Each row in result$table is one Person, Rater or Task element.
path <- system.file("extdata", "facets-example", package = "mfrmr")
result <- read_facets_results(path,
  facet_map = c("Person", "Rater", "Task"), source_version = "4.5.0")
summary(result) # Availability, not a model-adequacy assessment.
#>    Facet Rows Measures Infit Outfit AnchorFlagged Extreme UnknownStatus
#> 1 Person    6        6     3      3             1       3             0
#> 2  Rater    2        2     2      2             2       0             0
#> 3   Task    3        3     3      3             3       0             0
result$table[, c("Facet", "ElementID", "Label", "Estimate", "SourceStatus")]
#> # A tibble: 11 × 5
#>    Facet  ElementID Label Estimate SourceStatus
#>    <chr>  <chr>     <chr>    <dbl> <chr>       
#>  1 Person 1         1      -1.80   extreme_low 
#>  2 Person 2         2      -3.10   extreme_low 
#>  3 Person 3         3       5.49   extreme_high
#>  4 Person 4         4      -0.0623 estimated   
#>  5 Person 5         5      -1      anchored    
#>  6 Person 6         6       1.30   estimated   
#>  7 Rater  1         1      -0.4    anchored    
#>  8 Rater  2         2       0.4    anchored    
#>  9 Task   1         1      -0.8    anchored    
#> 10 Task   2         2       0      anchored    
#> 11 Task   3         3       0.8    anchored    
plot(result, type = "measure", facets = "Rater", draw = FALSE)
# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("plot.mfrm_facets_results", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
path <- system.file("extdata", "facets-example", package = "mfrmr")
result <- read_facets_results(path,
  facet_map = c("Person", "Rater", "Task"), source_version = "4.5.0")
plot(result, type = "measure", facets = "Person")
p <- plot(result, type = "infit_outfit", facets = "Rater", draw = FALSE)
plot_data(p, "plot_data")[, c("Label", "X", "Y", "Available", "Reason")]
plot_data(p, "notes")
# Display names are joined by facet and exported ID, never by row order.
labels <- data.frame(Facet = "Person", ElementID = c("1", "2"),
  DisplayLabel = c("Participant A", "Participant B"))
labelled <- plot(result, facets = "Person", label_map = labels, draw = FALSE)
plot_data(labelled, "plot_data")[, c("ElementID", "Label", "DisplayLabel")]
# A separate synthetic PCM analysis, with four exported scale curves.
graph_path <- system.file("extdata", "facets-graph-example", "graph.txt",
  package = "mfrmr")
curves <- read_facets_results(graph_file = graph_path, source_version = "4.5.0")
summary(curves, component = "curves")
plot(curves, type = "ccc", scales = 1)
expected <- plot_data(curves, "plot_data", type = "expected", scales = 1)
head(expected[, c("Scale", "Measure", "Value", "Available")])
} # }
